identity.name: RELAXO FOOT LTD.
identity.industry: Footwear / Affordable Consumer Durables & Mass Market Retail

summary.oneLiner: Revenue declined due to GST 12%->5% transition causing channel destocking, but EBITDA and PAT margins expanded due to cost control and full price pass-through; recovery expected from Q4FY26 as inventory clears and GST benefits fully flow through to consumers.

one-line thesis: Revenue declined due to GST 12%->5% transition causing channel destocking, but EBITDA and PAT margins expanded due to cost control and full price pass-through; recovery expected from Q4FY26 as inventory clears and GST benefits fully flow through to consumers.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -7.5% YoY (Q2FY26); EBITDA: -3.2% YoY, margin +129 bps to 12.9%; PAT: -2.7% YoY, margin +34 bps to 5.8%; order book: not disclosed; net debt: not disclosed - no one-offs or accounting distortions noted except for higher other income from treasury/hedging gains
guidance: Revenue growth: expected to turn positive in Q4FY26; margin: stable to expand; order inflow: not guided; capex/commissioning: INR100-150 crores FY26-FY27 for warehouse modernization, HO building, and operational efficiency - no capacity expansion planned
segment / subsidiary detail: Open footwear: 80% of sales; Closed footwear: 20% of sales; >98% of portfolio priced below INR2,500; >90% below INR1,000; Flite brand launching premium PU range; Sparx and Bahamas contribute 65% combined
growth verticals / optionality: Premiumization via Flite PU and athleisure sneakers; potential market share gain from unorganized sector due to GST 5% pricing advantage; RPA app driving 60% of secondary sales
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 129 bps YoY to 12.9% in Q2FY26 due to cost rationalization, back-end optimization, and full GST price pass-through; no margin compression from inverted duty structure expected as refund mechanism covers bulk impact
capex / expansion: INR100-150 crores for FY26-FY27; focused on warehouse modernization, HO building, moulds, plant renovations; no capacity expansion planned for next 18 months
capital allocation: Capex prioritized for operational efficiency over capacity expansion; no dividend or buyback guidance provided; focus on debt reduction and working capital optimization
risks & watch-items: Delayed inventory digestion beyond December 2025; inverted duty structure refund delays; persistent unorganized competition; consumer sentiment remains muted; regional variation in GST adoption speed
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; confident in GST 2.0 tailwinds; acknowledge near-term headwinds from channel destocking but expect recovery from Q4FY26; emphasize competitive positioning and cost discipline
non-obvious takeaways: Distributor trade discount remains fixed at 9% of wholesale price (not MRP), so absolute commission falls with lower MRP - but management believes volume growth offsets this; RPA app now drives 60% of secondary sales, indicating digital transformation is accelerating
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unorganized sector gains share due to tax arbitrage | Unorganized footwear players | loser | High | GST 5% removes their tax advantage; Relaxo now competitively priced below INR2,500 |
| Channel partners face lower absolute commission due to MRP reduction | Distributors and retailers | loser | Medium | Trade discount fixed at 9% of wholesale price; volume growth expected to compensate |

themes.title: Branded innerwear & domestic apparel
themes.need: Branded innerwear and domestic apparel are driven by rural recovery, GST 2.0 and distribution reach - a domestic-consumption thesis, not the China+1/FTA export tailwind powering exporters and synthetics.
themes.driver: Rural recovery + GST 2.0 demand pull and distribution-led volume growth.
